questions.question: A prepaid electricity tariff charges R1,95 per kWh for the first 150 kWh, R2,45 per kWh from 151 to 450 kWh, and R2,85 per kWh from 451 to 700 kWh. Calculate the cost of 420 kWh, and explain why multiplying 420 by R2,45 gives the wrong answer.
questions.expected_answer: Consumption fills the blocks in order. The first 150 kWh fall in block one: 150 × R1,95 = R292,50. The remaining 420 − 150 = 270 kWh fall in block two: 270 × R2,45 = R661,50. Block three is not reached. The total is 292,50 + 661,50 = R954,00. Multiplying all 420 units by R2,45 gives R1 029,00, which is R75,00 too much, because a block's rate applies only to the units inside that block — the first 150 units keep block one's cheaper price of R1,95 even though total consumption reached into block two.

questions.question: A water tariff supplies the first 6 kl free, charges R16,80 per kl from 6 to 20 kl, and R29,50 per kl from 20 to 35 kl. Calculate the amount payable for 26 kl including VAT at 15%, showing how many kilolitres are charged in each block.
questions.expected_answer: The first 6 kl are free. The middle block runs from 6 to 20 kl, a capacity of 20 − 6 = 14 kl, all of which is used: 14 × R16,80 = R235,20. The remaining 26 − 20 = 6 kl fall in the top block: 6 × R29,50 = R177,00. The check is that 6 + 14 + 6 = 26 kl, matching the meter. The consumption subtotal is 235,20 + 177,00 = R412,20. VAT is applied once, on the subtotal: 412,20 × 0,15 = R61,83 to the nearest cent. The amount payable is 412,20 + 61,83 = R474,03. The free block carries no VAT because its charge is zero.

questions.question: A household can use the prepaid rising block tariff or a conventional option costing R250,00 fixed per month plus a flat R1,90 per kWh. Compare the two options at 420 kWh and at 650 kWh, and advise which option suits which kind of household, referring to the idea of a break-even point.
questions.expected_answer: At 420 kWh: prepaid costs R954,00 (150 × 1,95 + 270 × 2,45), while conventional costs 420 × 1,90 = R798,00 plus R250,00, giving R1 048,00 — prepaid is cheaper by R94,00. At 650 kWh: prepaid costs 292,50 + 300 × 2,45 + 200 × 2,85 = 292,50 + 735,00 + 570,00 = R1 597,50, while conventional costs 650 × 1,90 = R1 235,00 plus R250,00, giving R1 485,00 — conventional is cheaper by R112,50. The advice depends on consumption: low users should stay on prepaid because the fixed charge spread over few units makes conventional expensive, while heavy users should choose conventional because the flat rate avoids the expensive upper blocks. Between 420 and 650 kWh lies the break-even consumption, where both options cost the same; on a graph of cost against consumption it is the point where the two cost lines cross, with prepaid lying lower below the crossing and conventional lower above it.
